findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 5 projects, synced last week." is followed by a list of only four items: Support Backlog Triage, Beta Launch Plan, Partner Integration Pilot, Mobile App Revamp.
findings.fix: Add the fifth project to the list, or correct the summary text to say "4 projects."
findings.location: Workspace overview section (id="workspace-overview"), the summary paragraph above the project list.
findings.violation: The stated count of 5 projects does not match the 4 projects actually listed, so either the summary text is wrong or a project is missing from the list.

findings.evidence: The four project names appear only as plain list items with no href or button attached, while the single link "Open project settings" (id="workspace-overview-projects-link") is not associated with any of them.
findings.fix: Make each project name a link or button that opens settings for that specific project.
findings.location: Workspace overview section (id="workspace-overview"), the project list and the "Open project settings" link.
findings.violation: There is no way to open a specific project from the list, and it is unclear which project "Open project settings" is meant to open.

findings.evidence: The input is id="project-settings-name-input" with value="Customer Migration".
findings.fix: Populate the settings page with the project the user actually selected, or add "Customer Migration" to the projects list so the two screens agree.
findings.location: Project settings section (id="project-settings"), the "Project name" input.
findings.violation: "Customer Migration" is not one of the four projects shown in "Your projects," so a user who clicked "Open project settings" from the overview lands on settings for a project they cannot identify from the list they just saw.

findings.evidence: The button is id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" with aria-label="Duplicate project" and no visible text between its opening and closing tags.
findings.fix: Add visible text or an icon to the button so its purpose is clear to sighted users, not only to screen readers.
findings.location: Project settings section (id="project-settings"), the duplicate button.
findings.violation: The button has an aria-label but no visible text or icon, so sighted users see an empty control and cannot tell what it does or that it is interactive.

findings.evidence: The link id="project-settings-archive-link" points to href="#project-archived", and no link anywhere in the document points to the "Archive this project?" section, id="archive-confirm".
findings.fix: Point "Archive project" at "#archive-confirm" instead of "#project-archived" so the confirmation step is actually part of the flow.
findings.location: Project settings section (id="project-settings"), the "Archive project" link.
findings.violation: A confirmation step exists in the document but is unreachable, so clicking "Archive project" performs the archive action immediately with no chance to confirm or cancel.

findings.evidence: The form ends with a Save button, id="invite-member-save-btn", type="submit", and separately, outside the form, a Continue link, id="invite-member-continue-link", href="#invite-sent".
findings.fix: Combine them into a single action, for example by making the Save button itself lead to the invite-sent confirmation, and remove the redundant Continue link.
findings.location: Invite a team member section (id="invite-member"), the form's Save button and the Continue link.
findings.violation: It is unclear whether Save or Continue is what actually sends the invite, since two separate controls appear to do the same job with no stated relationship between them.

findings.evidence: The input id="invite-member-email-input" has no "required" attribute, and "Continue," id="invite-member-continue-link", links to "#invite-sent" independently of the form.
findings.fix: Make Continue the form's actual submit action and mark the email field as required, so an invite cannot be confirmed without an address.
findings.location: Invite a team member section (id="invite-member"), the email input and the Continue link.
findings.violation: A user can reach the "Invite sent" confirmation by clicking Continue even with the email field left blank, since Continue does not depend on the form being filled in or submitted.

findings.evidence: The select has three options, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and none of them is marked selected.
findings.fix: Mark the option matching the user's current digest frequency with the "selected" attribute.
findings.location: Notification settings section (id="notification-settings"), the "Digest frequency" select.
findings.violation: With no option marked selected, the control defaults to showing "Daily" regardless of the user's actual current setting, which will misrepresent their preference if it is really Weekly or Monthly.

findings.evidence: The button id="project-settings-save-btn", type="submit", labeled "Save," has no corresponding result or confirmation section anywhere in the document.
findings.fix: Add a confirmation state or inline success message after saving the project name, matching the confirmation pattern used for invites and archiving.
findings.location: Project settings section (id="project-settings"), the Save button for the project name.
findings.violation: Unlike the invite and archive flows, which both show an explicit confirmation screen after their action, saving the project name gives the user no feedback that the change took effect.

findings.evidence: The button id="notification-settings-save-btn", type="submit", labeled "Submit," has no corresponding result or confirmation section.
findings.fix: Add a confirmation state or inline success message after submitting notification settings.
findings.location: Notification settings section (id="notification-settings"), the Submit button.
findings.violation: As with the project name Save button, submitting notification preferences gives no confirmation that the change was saved, unlike the invite and archive flows.

findings.evidence: The notification settings form uses the label "Submit," while the project settings and invite member forms both use the label "Save" for their submit buttons.
findings.fix: Use "Save" for all three form submit buttons instead of "Submit" for one of them.
findings.location: Notification settings section (id="notification-settings"), the Submit button label.
findings.violation: Using a different label for the same kind of action, saving a form, makes the interface feel inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "The last import finished with 3 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 63, 71, and 82 were skipped; every other row was imported."
findings.fix: State the total row count, for example "82 of 85 rows were imported."
findings.location: Import status section (id="import-status"), the status message.
findings.violation: The message never states the total number of rows in the import, so "every other row was imported" cannot be verified or understood in context.
